title: Dry weather and drought in England: 23 to 29 October 2026

details.body:
1. Summary

Two named storms, Austen and Boelo, made this the wettest reporting week across England since October 2024.

2. Active temporary use bans (TUBs)

The following companies have implemented TUBs, in all or part of their supply areas:

  • Affinity Water – central and east regions, covering Bedfordshire, Berkshire, Buckinghamshire, Hertfordshire, Surrey, and parts of London and Essex
  • Anglian Water – whole company area, excluding Hartlepool
  • Bristol Water – whole company area
  • Cambridge Water – whole company area
  • Essex and Suffolk Water – whole company area
  • Southern Water – Hampshire and the Isle of Wight
  • South East Water – whole company area
  • South West Water – whole company area, excluding Bournemouth
  • Thames Water – whole company area
  • Wessex Water – whole company area

The Water Industry Act 1991 incorporates legislation which makes provision for another water undertaker to supply sites within an existing water undertaker’s area. Where an alternative undertaker is appointed, a New Appointment and Variation (NAV) is made by Ofwat. Companies operating as a NAV have the same legal duties and responsibilities as other water companies to produce drought plans. NAVs can have their own sources of supply but are primarily supplied by bulk supply agreements with the water undertaker in the area. NAV TUBs were introduced at the same time as their respective incumbent companies as follows:

  • Leaf Water implemented TUBs for its customers in areas supplied by South East Water, Essex and Suffolk Water, and Cambridge Water

  • Albion Water implemented TUBs for its customers in areas supplied by Thames Water

  • Leep Water implemented TUBs for its customers in areas supplied by South East Water, Southern Water, South West Water, Thames Water, Wessex Water, Anglian Water, Affinity Water, Bristol Water, and Essex and Suffolk Water

  • Independent Water Networks (IWN) implemented TUBs for its customers in areas supplied by South East Water, Southern Water, South West Water, Thames Water, Wessex Water, Anglian Water, Affinity Water, Bristol Water, Cambridge Water, and Essex and Suffolk Water

  • Last Mile Water implemented TUBs for its customers in areas supplied by South East Water, Southern Water, South West Water, Anglian Water, Affinity Water, Thames Water, Essex and Suffolk Water, Wessex Water and Bristol Water

  • MUA implemented TUBs for its customers in areas supplied by Affinity Water and Anglian Water

  • ESP implemented TUBs for its customers in areas supplied by Bristol Water, Wessex Water, Thames Water, South East Water, Affinity Water and Anglian Water

  • Matrix implemented TUBs for its customers in areas supplied by Thames Water

Further information can be found on each company’s website.

3. Environment Agency Area drought status

There have been two changes in Environment Agency Area drought status this week:

  • Cumbria and Lancashire moved to recovery on 28 October
  • Greater Manchester, Merseyside and Cheshire moved to recovery on 28 October

Figure 1: Environment Agency drought status

3.1 Environment Agency Areas in severe drought

  • Parts of Devon and Cornwall and Wessex Areas that are supplied by Wimbleball reservoir, Kenninck, Tottisford & Trenchford (KTT) and Venford reservoirs, and Stithians and Drift reservoirs
  • Parts of Solent and South Downs and Kent and South London Areas that are supplied by Ardingly reservoir

3.2 Environment Agency Areas in drought

  • Remaining parts of Devon, Cornwall and Isles of Scilly that are not in severe drought

  • Remaining parts of Wessex that are not in severe drought

  • Remaining parts of Kent and South London that are not in severe drought

  • Remaining parts of Solent and South Downs that are not in severe drought

  • East Anglia

  • Hertfordshire and North London

  • Thames

  • West Midlands

  • East Midlands

  • Lincolnshire and Northamptonshire
  • Yorkshire
